title: Manual order syncing between two systems
honesty_boundary: This tool is a scoping aid for checkable trial definitions, not a guarantee of outcomes. Synthetic demo claims describe fictional examples and no real engagements. Evidence pointers are supplied by the input and are not independently inspected.
problem: A shop manually compares two order exports and needs a concise review list of records that differ.

artifact.name: Two-export order comparison bundle
artifact.format: A runnable standard-library comparator and CSV/JSON result files.
artifact.scope_limit: The artifact is limited to the mapped capabilities and listed acceptance criteria.

mapped_claims.claim: compare order records across two exports

acceptance_criteria.condition: comparison-summary.json reports exactly 25 left records, 25 right records, 22 matched records, and 3 mismatched records.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Parse comparison-summary.json and compare each count with the 4 specified values.

acceptance_criteria.condition: mismatches.csv contains exactly 3 data rows and the columns order_id, left_status, right_status, mismatch_reason.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Count mismatches.csv rows and compare its header with the 4 required column names.

acceptance_criteria.condition: matched.csv contains exactly 22 data rows, with one row per matching order_id.
acceptance_criteria.verification_method: Count matched.csv data rows and verify that order_id values are unique.

assumptions: The buyer supplies two UTF-8 CSV exports with 25 records each and a shared order_id field.
Status values can be compared as exact text after trimming surrounding whitespace.
exclusions: No write-back to either commerce or fulfilment system.
No automatic resolution of mismatches or live synchronisation service.

fixed_price.pricing_rule: GBP 750 per day plus GBP 125 per acceptance criterion; day count follows the documented scope threshold.
